spec.name: L-shaped bracket, plane strain, clamped base, pressure on top of vertical leg
spec.geometry: L-shaped domain, union of the unit squares [0,1]x[0,1], [1,2]x[0,1] and [0,1]x[1,2] (side 1 m). Outer corners are (0,0), (2,0), (2,1), (1,1), (1,2), (0,2). The re-entrant corner is at (1,1), with an interior angle of 270°. The domain is modelled per unit thickness (plane strain).
spec.material: Hyperelastic, plane strain, Poisson's ratio 0.25. The strain-energy model (for example compressible neo-Hookean or Saint Venant–Kirchhoff) is not given, and neither is the stiffness scale (Young's modulus E or shear modulus μ). With ν = 0.25 the material is far from incompressible, so volumetric locking is not expected.
spec.loading: Uniform pressure p = 5 kPa on the top edge y = 2, 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 (the top of the vertical leg), acting downward and normal to the edge. The bottom edge y = 0, 0 ≤ x ≤ 2, is clamped (u = 0). All other edges are traction-free: x = 0 for 0 ≤ y ≤ 2; x = 2 and y = 1 for 1 ≤ x ≤ 2; x = 1 for 1 ≤ y ≤ 2. It is not stated whether the pressure is a follower load or a dead load, or whether it is applied in increments.
qois: Total strain energy per unit thickness (global; converges under refinement despite the corner singularities, at a rate limited by the re-entrant-corner exponent instead of the smooth-solution rate)

Vertical displacement u_y at the point (0, 2), the top-left corner of the vertical leg (displacement is continuous and bounded; converges under refinement, possibly at a reduced rate from the singularities)
well_posedness: Dirichlet condition: the clamp on y = 0 over the whole base (0 ≤ x ≤ 2) removes all rigid-body modes, so the boundary value problem is well posed.
Neumann data: the pressure on y = 2 (0 ≤ x ≤ 1) is bounded and uniform. All remaining edges are traction-free.

Re-entrant corner at (1,1) with a 270° interior angle: the linearized stress is singular, roughly r^(λ-1) with λ ≈ 0.544. Pointwise or peak stress near (1,1) will not converge and must not be used as a QoI. Strain energy and displacements still converge, but at a reduced algebraic rate, so uniform Q4 will not reach O(h^2) in L2 or O(h) in energy.

Clamped–free corners at (0,0) and (2,0), where the clamped base meets the free edges x = 0 and x = 2 at 90°, produce weaker stress singularities that depend on ν. These also rule out peak stress as a QoI there.

Corners at the ends of the loaded edge, (0,2) and (1,2), where pressure meets a traction-free edge: the traction jump gives local non-smoothness. The displacement at (0,2) is still well defined because the displacement field is continuous.
Material stability: ν = 0.25 is far from the incompressible limit. Polyconvexity or ellipticity of the strain-energy function cannot be confirmed until the hyperelastic model is specified.

Load level vs limit points: whether p = 5 kPa is small or large depends on the unspecified stiffness. The vertical leg is stocky (aspect ratio 1:1) and under compression, so buckling or a limit point is unlikely at moderate p/E. This must still be checked with an incremental load path, monitoring the tangent stiffness (determinant / smallest eigenvalue) and det F > 0 everywhere.
Uniqueness: under small load relative to stiffness, the nonlinear solution stays near the unique linear-elastic branch. Uniqueness is not guaranteed if p/E is large.
open_questions: Which hyperelastic strain-energy function is used (neo-Hookean, Saint Venant–Kirchhoff, Mooney–Rivlin, ...)?
What are Young's modulus E (or shear modulus μ) and the bulk modulus? Without them, the load level p/E and the size of the nonlinearity cannot be judged.
Is the 5 kPa pressure a follower load (normal to the deformed edge) or a dead load (fixed downward traction)?
Which element type and mesh family are used? Q4 was assumed as the default. Is the refinement uniform, or graded toward the re-entrant corner at (1,1)?
Is there an independent reference value (overkill mesh, higher-order or adaptive solution) for the energy and u_y(0,2), or should the reference be extrapolated from the refinement family?
Confirm that 'clamped' means u_x = u_y = 0 on the whole bottom edge 0 ≤ x ≤ 2.
Is the strain energy reported per unit thickness (J/m), and is the sign convention for u_y positive upward?
Load stepping and Newton tolerance used, so that discretization error can be separated from solver error.
